findings.title: join breaks early on deadline and skips terminating remaining processes
findings.body: In join(), the loop over processes uses `break` once the deadline has passed. Every process not yet visited is then never terminated. Those processes are daemon processes and keep running, flushing Redis and producing to Kafka after shutdown or across rebalances. With many shards, they can pile up as orphaned flushers.

findings.title: isinstance check against multiprocessing.Process misses SpawnProcess
findings.body: The processes are created through `get_context('spawn').Process`, so they are `SpawnProcess` instances. That class derives from `multiprocessing.process.BaseProcess`, not from `multiprocessing.Process`. The checks `isinstance(process, multiprocessing.Process)` are therefore always False. As a result, hung processes are never killed before a replacement is spawned, and join never terminates processes. This differs from the old code, which called kill unconditionally.

findings.title: Zero assigned shards causes modulo-by-zero / empty map
findings.body: If a consumer is assigned no partitions, `buffer.assigned_shards` is empty. `max_processes` then falls back to 0 and `num_processes` is 0. No flusher runs, and the loop is empty, so the modulo-by-zero is never hit. However, passing `--flusher-processes 0` while shards are assigned makes `num_processes` 0 and raises ZeroDivisionError in `i % self.num_processes`.

findings.title: Default flusher_processes=1 contradicts per-shard intent
findings.body: The CLI default of 1 is always passed to the factory, so the `max_processes or len(shards)` fallback (one process per shard) is never reached in production. The PR description says the flusher spawns a process per shard, and the class docstring says it creates one process per shard. Both are wrong for the default configuration, which still runs a single flusher process.

findings.title: Inconsistent metric tag key 'shards' vs 'shard'
findings.body: The `wait_produce` timer uses the tag key `shards`, while the neighbouring metrics use `shard`. This inconsistency breaks dashboards and queries that group by the shard tag.
